artifacts.summary: Five-phase plan to create the sapience extension in the source store: manifest plus permission grants (gap 1), EXTENSION.md wrapup instruction (gap 2), four domain notes (gap 3 documented), index entries, then activate/redeploy/verify.

memory_candidates.content: An extension lifecycle hook declared in manifest.json's top-level `hooks` object can NEVER fire for an extension that declares no `task_type`. `skill_get_extension_dir()` in agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/skill-base.sh gates on `[ -n "$ext_task_type" ] && [ "$ext_task_type" = "$task_type" ]` and returns the FIRST matching extension, and all four call sites of `skill_run_extension_hook` (preflight, context_injection, verification, postflight) pass the CURRENT task's own TASK_TYPE. So nvim/nix context-injection hooks work only because each declares its own matching task_type and fires only on its own domain's tasks. There is no extension-declarable seam for cross-cutting, task-type-independent pre-dispatch injection: the one instance of that shape (<memory-context>) is a hardcoded memory-retrieve.sh call inside core's own orchestrate-build-dispatch.sh. Post-task observers are also wrong for pre-work orientation -- they fire only after a task reaches a resting state.
